entries.name: Shouting
entries.description: The adult raises their voice to a shout or yells at the child.

entries.name: Demanding eye contact
entries.description: The adult tells or pressures the child to look at them, for example "look at me".

entries.name: Staring
entries.description: The adult keeps looking intently at the child's face for several seconds without a break.

entries.name: Rapid-fire questions
entries.description: The adult asks several questions in quick succession without giving the child time to process or answer.

entries.name: Long multi-step instructions
entries.description: The adult gives a long instruction with several steps at once.

entries.name: Sarcasm or vague language
entries.description: The adult uses sarcasm, idioms or vague language the child may take literally.

entries.name: Anger or impatience
entries.description: The adult sounds angry, irritated or impatient with the child.

entries.name: Pressuring speech
entries.description: The adult pushes the child to speak or respond, for example "say hello!".

entries.name: Moving too close or too fast
entries.description: The adult moves into the child's personal space or approaches quickly.

entries.name: Reaching toward or touching
entries.description: The adult reaches toward the child, makes a sudden movement at them, or touches them.

entries.name: Demands during a meltdown
entries.description: The adult asks questions or gives instructions while the child is in a meltdown.

entries.name: Calm, quiet voice
entries.description: The adult speaks calmly and quietly in short, simple sentences.

entries.name: Waiting quietly
entries.description: The adult stays quiet and gives the child time.

entries.name: Letting the child look away
entries.description: The adult lets the child look away without remarking on it or asking for eye contact.

entries.name: Giving space
entries.description: The adult keeps a comfortable distance from the child.
